program_rules.applies_to: next $4,000,000 recovered (above the first $1,000,000)
program_rules.quote: The declarant shall be entitled to 20 percent to 30 percent of any recovery up to the first $1,000,000 recovered, 10 percent to 20 percent of the next $4,000,000 recovered, and 5 percent to 10 percent of the next $5,000,000 recovered.
program_rules.notes: Second tier of the sliding scale; the first tier (20-30% of the first $1,000,000) is already recorded.

events.title: Lacey Act Amendments of 1981: rewards from fines and forfeitures
events.description: Section 6 of the Lacey Act Amendments of 1981 (16 U.S.C. 3375(d)) directs the Interior or Treasury Secretary to pay, beginning in fiscal year 1983, a reward from penalties, fines or forfeitures to anyone whose information leads to an arrest, conviction, civil penalty or forfeiture; amount set by the Secretary; officials ineligible.

events.title: Reduced or no share for relators who planned the fraud

new_indicators.name: Cases handled by the agency enforcing a reward law

ledger.contains: Joint Annual Interagency Coordination Report of the Texas HHSC Inspector General and the Attorney General for state fiscal years 2015 and 2016 (6 pp.): coordination activities; key-metrics tables for the HHSC Inspector General (screenings, investigations, referrals, recoveries) and the AG's criminal Medicaid Fraud Control Unit (referrals, cases, convictions, fines and restitution) - both out of scope, they are not the reward programme; the AG's Civil Medicaid Fraud Division table (cases opened, closed, pending, total recovered) for FY2015 and FY2016; 12 matters with recoveries of $2 million or higher named with amounts; ongoing cases (Xerox, dental providers, AstraZeneca) without amounts. The two recovery totals were already recorded. Added the division case counts (6, proposed indicator enforcement_matters), the count of 12 large matters, and as cases the 7 large matters that involve a relator (ex rel. caption or 'relator portions'). Not added as cases: Perrigo ($15,000,000), Breckenridge ($12,500,000), Prasco ($6,950,000), Ranbaxy ($39,750,000) and Glenmark ($25,000,000), which the report lists as Texas investigations or suits with only state and federal portions (no whistleblower).

Joint Annual Interagency Coordination Report, Texas state fiscal year 2017 (5 pp., scanned, read by OCR at 300 dpi): coordination activities; HHSC Inspector General and Medicaid Fraud Control Unit key metrics (out of scope); Civil Medicaid Fraud Division table (cases opened 113, closed 66, pending 468, recovered $48,988,225.35); five matters with recoveries of $2 million or higher; ongoing cases (Xerox, dental providers, AstraZeneca, CVS, Lupin) without amounts. The recovery total was already recorded. Added the three case counts, the count of 5 large matters and the 3 large matters involving a relator as cases. Not added as cases: Dava ($9,523,919.47) and Cypress ($2,000,000), state and federal portions only.

Joint Annual Interagency Coordination Report, Texas state fiscal year 2018 (5 pp.): coordination activities; OIG and MFCU key metrics (out of scope); Civil Medicaid Fraud Division table (cases opened 86, closed 102, pending 456, recovered $185,688,277.89); six matters of $2 million or more, all with relator portions; ongoing cases without amounts. Recovery total already recorded. Added the three case counts, the count of 6 large matters and the 6 matters as cases (relators named in the captions).

Joint Annual Interagency Coordination Report, Texas state fiscal year 2019 (6 pp.): coordination activities; OIG key metrics and five OIG settlements, MFCU key metrics (out of scope: not the reward programme); Civil Medicaid Fraud Division table (cases opened 97, closed 85, pending 445, recovered $163,692,156.95); five matters of $2 million or more; CVS and Lupin resolved but not finalised; ongoing cases without amounts. Joint Annual Interagency Coordination Report, Texas state fiscal year 2020 (5 pp.): coordination activities; OIG and MFCU key metrics (out of scope); Civil Medicaid Fraud Division table (cases opened 105, closed 36, pending 514, recovered $236,033,459.42); six named matters of $2 million or more ('several', no count); ongoing cases (dental providers, Malouf judgment on appeal, Janssen) without amounts. Joint Annual Interagency Coordination Report, Texas state fiscal year 2021 (6 pp.): coordination activities; OIG and MFCU key metrics (out of scope); Civil Medicaid Fraud Division table (cases opened 85, closed 0, pending 421, recovered $52,160,120.06) with a footnote on 178 cases pending physical closure; nine matters of $2 million or more, all with relator portions; ongoing cases (Malouf $16 million judgment on appeal, Janssen, LabCorp). Joint Annual Interagency Coordination Report, Texas state fiscal year 2022 (6 pp.): coordination activities; OIG and MFCU key metrics (out of scope); Civil Medicaid Fraud Division table (cases opened 73, closed 163, pending 387, recovered $79,536,460.66); seven matters of $2 million or more; ongoing cases (Malouf, LabCorp). Texas Attorney General press release of 8 Aug 2023: the Civil Medicaid Fraud Division settled a TMFPA action, first brought by a whistleblower under the qui tam provisions, against Shire, Baxter, Baxalta, Viropharma and Takeda entities ($42.7 million in the headline, 'more than $42 million' in the text); cumulative recoveries of about $2.5 billion since 2000 (already recorded). The rest of the page is site navigation and links to unrelated criminal Medicaid fraud releases (out of scope). Added the settlement as a case.

12 U.S.C. 4201 (2024 ed.): any person may file a declaration of a FIRREA bank-fraud violation (civil penalties under 12 U.S.C. 1833a) with the Attorney General; credits (Pub. L. 101-647, 29 Nov 1990) and the short title (Financial Institutions Anti-Fraud Enforcement Act of 1990). No numbers. The enactment event is already recorded from this source; nothing else in scope. Nothing added.

12 U.S.C. 4205 (2024 ed.): rights of FIRREA declarants: choice of private counsel; discretionary reward after a criminal conviction with eight factors; mandatory share of civil recoveries on a sliding scale (20-30% of the first $1,000,000, 10-20% of the next $4,000,000, 5-10% of the next $5,000,000); multiple declarants; banking-agency exception; 2002 amendment notes (former $5,000-$100,000 conviction reward and repealed subsec. (e)). Already recorded: the first-tier 20-30% and the civil-share mandatory flag. Added the second and third tiers (4 rules), the former $5,000 minimum and $100,000 cap (1990-2002), the discretionary flag for conviction rewards since 2002, and the 2002 rule-change event.

15 U.S.C. 78u-6 (Exchange Act sec. 21F, 2023 ed.): definitions (covered action over $1,000,000; monetary sanctions; original information; related action), awards of 10-30% of collected sanctions, criteria and exclusions, representation (anonymous claims through counsel), appeals within 30 days, the Investor Protection Fund (deposit unless the balance exceeds $300,000,000; Fair Fund amounts unless that fund exceeds $200,000,000), annual report to Congress, anti-retaliation (6/3/10-year limits, 2 times back pay), confidentiality, false information. Already recorded: 10% min, 30% max, $1,000,000 threshold, $300,000,000 fund threshold. Added discretionary, anonymous filing, 30-day appeal and the 6-year retaliation limit. Not added: the $200,000,000 disgorgement-fund condition (noted in the existing Dodd-Frank fund row), 2x back pay (no rule type; in notes). The 2010 launch event already exists from other sources.

16 U.S.C. 3375 (Lacey Act enforcement, 2024 ed.): enforcement agencies and powers, district-court jurisdiction, and (d) rewards from penalties, fines or forfeitures beginning in fiscal year 1983 (amount set by the Secretary; officials ineligible) plus costs of caring for seized wildlife; amendment notes (1984, 1988). No numbers. The discretionary rule was already recorded; added the 1981 enactment event and a suggested correction of the rule's start date (FY1983 began 1 Oct 1982).

26 U.S.C. 7623 (2023 ed., 4 pp., also printing 7621 and 7624): (a) discretionary payments for detecting underpayments; (b) mandatory awards of 15-30% of proceeds collected, at most 10% for cases based on public disclosures, reduction or denial for planners, 30-day Tax Court appeal, $200,000 gross-income and $2,000,000 thresholds, perjury attestation; (c) definition of proceeds incl. criminal fines and forfeitures (2018); (d) anti-retaliation (180-day complaint, 200% back pay); amendment and effective-date notes (1996, 2006, 2018, 2019); statutory notes on the Whistleblower Office and annual reports; 7624 reimbursement of state and local agencies (up to 10% of taxes recovered, not a whistleblower programme, out of scope). Already recorded: 15/30/10%, 200% back pay, 180 days, $200,000, $2,000,000 (2018), anonymous 0, and the 1996 and 2019 events. Added the 30-day appeal, the mandatory-award flag, the 2018 fines-in-proceeds flag and the pre-2018 $2,000,000 threshold. Events for 2006 and 2018 already exist from other sources, so none added.

31 U.S.C. 3730 (2023 ed., 5 pp., with the end of 3729 notes and 3731-3732): Attorney General and qui tam actions (complaint under seal at least 60 days, government election), rights of the parties, relator shares (15-25% if the government proceeds, at most 10% if based primarily on public disclosures, 25-30% if not), reduction for planners, barred actions and the public-disclosure bar, retaliation relief (2x back pay, 3-year limit), historical and amendment notes (1986, 1988, 2009, 2010, 2022); 3731 limitation periods (6/3/10 years) and 3732 jurisdiction. Already recorded: 15% and 25% minimums, mandatory flag, public-disclosure bar, the 2010 ACA event. Added the three maximums (25%, 30%, 10%), the 3-year retaliation limit and the 1988 event. Events for 1986, 2009 and July 2010 already exist from other sources. Not recorded: seal and intervention periods and FCA limitation periods (no rule type).

31 U.S.C. 5323 'Rewards for informants' (2018 ed.): the Secretary may pay a reward for original information leading to a recovery over $50,000 for a BSA violation; at most 25% of the net amount collected or $150,000, whichever is less; officials ineligible; appropriations authorised (no amount). All in-scope rules (threshold, two caps, discretionary) and the 1984 enactment event are already recorded from this source. Nothing added.

31 U.S.C. 5323 'Whistleblower incentives and protections' (2021 ed., as rewritten by the AML Act of 2020): definitions (covered action over $1,000,000), awards up to 30% subject to appropriations, discretion and exclusions, anonymous claims through counsel, 30-day appeal, anti-retaliation (Labor complaint, 180 days, 6/3/10 years, 2x back pay), confidentiality, false information, rulemaking, no waiver. Already recorded: 30% max, $1,000,000 threshold, discretionary. Added anonymous filing, 30-day appeal and the 6-year retaliation limit. The 2021 rewrite event already exists twice from other sources; none added.

31 U.S.C. 5323 (2023 ed., after the AML Whistleblower Improvement Act, Pub. L. 117-328, 29 Dec 2022): covered actions under the BSA, IEEPA, TWEA and Kingpin Act over $1,000,000; mandatory awards of 10-30% from the Financial Integrity Fund (deposits stop above $300,000,000); smaller awards allowed for related actions paid by another programme; discretion, exclusions, anonymous claims, 30-day appeal, anti-retaliation, confidentiality; amendment notes with the 2021 text of (b). Already recorded: 10%, 30%, $1,000,000, $300,000,000. Added discretionary, anonymous filing, 30-day appeal and the 6-year retaliation limit. The Dec 2022 event already exists twice from other sources. Not recorded: the related-action exception to the 10% minimum (5323(b)(2)(B), no amount).
